newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Prince William slammed for killing stag.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Prince William slammed for killing stag.

text.p: Animal rights activists on Wednesday accused Princess Diana's eldest son Prince William of having his hands "awash with blood" after a newspaper reported he had stalked and shot his first stag.

The Daily Telegraph said the 14-year-old prince made the kill last month on Queen Elizabeth's Balmoral estate in the Scottish Highlands. He was accompanied by his 12-year-old brother Harry and his father Prince Charles.
Les Ward, director of the Edinburgh-based animal rights group Advocates For Animals, condemned both Charles and the young prince.
"It is absolutely disgusting that any father should take his young son to shoot and kill an animal," he said.
"His hands (William's) are awash with blood. It goes against public opinion and shows a total disrespect for animal life."
The League Against Cruel Sports said culling of deer should be done by professionals, not treated as a "sporting accessory" by the royal family.
"They seem to be bringing up the prince with brutal, dreadful morals," said spokesman Kevin Saunders.

The Daily Telegraph said that after the kill, the stag would have been "gralloched" -- disembowelled with a large knife -- in order to prevent the carcass from bloating and to make it easier to be dragged away.

Prince Charles is a keen hunter, as is Tiggy Legge-Bourke, the aide who is responsible for looking after his sons when they are with him. Princess Diana, who was divorced from Charles in August, has no taste for blood sports.
Legge-Bourke has helped the young princes practise their marksmanship by shooting rabbits and crows.
